title: Lower semicontinuity of geometric component counts in flat proper families
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper flat morphism of finite presentation of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-flat-morphism] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $s\in S$, write $X_{\bar s}=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}$ for its geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Let $n(s)$ be the number of connected components (maximal nonempty connected subsets) of its underlying space [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Each $n(s)$ is finite, with $n(s)=0$ when $X_{\bar s}$ is empty. For every $s\in S$ there is an open neighbourhood $V$ of $s$ such that $n(t)\geq n(s)$ for every $t\in V$; equivalently, the integer-valued function $n$ is lower semicontinuous.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and replace $S$ by an affine open neighbourhood of $s$, pulling back $X$. This does not change any fibre at a point of that open. Properness is preserved by this base change. Flatness and local finite presentation restrict because the same stalk maps and affine presentation witnesses are used. Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Take the canonical Stein factorization $X\xrightarrow{q}T=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\xrightarrow{\pi}S$. The affine Stein theorem gives that $\pi$ is integral and $q$ is proper with geometrically connected, hence nonempty, fibres. The Stein-fibre lemma gives finitely many points of $T$ over $s$, all with finite residue extensions.

Apply integral-fibre etale splitting to $\pi:T\to S$ at $s$. Its two extra hypotheses are exactly the finiteness and residue-extension conclusions of step 1. Obtain an affine etale $g:U\to S$, $u$ over $s$, and $T_U=T\times_SU=\coprod_{i=1}^m V_i$, with each $V_i$ open and closed and having a single point $v_i$ over $u$ with purely inseparable residue extension. Set $X_U=X\times_SU$ and $X_i=q_U^{-1}(V_i)$, where $q_U:X_U\to T_U$ is the base change of $q$. Preimages of open-and-closed subsets are open and closed; they form a finite disjoint partition of $X_U$.

For every $w\in U$, base-change invariance gives $n_{X_U/U}(w)=n_{X/S}(g(w))$, in particular equality at $u$ and $s$. The morphism $X_U\to U$ is flat by flat base-change stability, and locally of finite presentation by the finite-presentation permanence theorem. Consequently each open subscheme $X_i$ is flat and locally of finite presentation over $U$: its stalk maps are those of $X_U\to U$, and if $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is an affine presentation witness at a point of $X_i$, choose a principal open $D(h)$ containing that point and contained in $X_i$. If $C=R[x_1,\ldots,x_a]/(r_1,\ldots,r_b)$, then $C_h=R[x_1,\ldots,x_a,z]/(r_1,\ldots,r_b,zh-1)$ is again finitely presented over $R$.

Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(u)$. The fibre $(V_i)_u\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ is injective on points and has a purely inseparable residue extension at its only point, so it is radicial. The radicial/universally-injective equivalence implies that $(V_i)_{\bar u}$ has at most one point. It has at least one: in positive characteristic send each $a\in\kappa(v_i)$, with $a^{p^r}=c\in\kappa(u)$, to the unique root of $Z^{p^r}-c$ in $\Omega$. Uniqueness makes this independent of the exponent; choosing a common exponent for two elements and using $(a+b)^{p^r}=a^{p^r}+b^{p^r}$ shows that it preserves sums, and the corresponding product identity shows it preserves products. It fixes $\kappa(u)$ and sends $1$ to $1$, so it is an injective field homomorphism. In characteristic zero the extension is trivial. Composing $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v_i)$ with the residue-field point gives an $\Omega$-point of $(V_i)_u$. Thus $(V_i)_{\bar u}$ has exactly one point $z_i$. The fibre of $q_\Omega$ at $z_i$ is a field extension of the fibre of $q$ at the image of $z_i$ in $T$: this follows by reassociating the fibre products. That fibre is connected and nonempty by the geometrically-connected-fibre clause of the affine Stein theorem and the definition of geometric connectedness. The fibre homeomorphism identifies its underlying space with $q_\Omega^{-1}(z_i)$, which is the whole of $(X_i)_{\bar u}$. Hence $(X_i)_{\bar u}$ is connected and nonempty.

The geometric fibre $(X_U)_{\bar u}$ is partitioned into the $m$ pairwise disjoint open-and-closed connected nonempty subsets $(X_i)_{\bar u}$. Each is a maximal connected subset: a connected subset cannot meet both an open-and-closed piece and its complement. Thus its component count is exactly $m$, and step 3 gives $n(s)=m<\infty$. This argument works at every $s$, proving finiteness everywhere. For $m=0$ the partition is empty, the geometric fibre is empty and $n(s)=0$. In that case the required inequality is automatic on $S$ because all counts are nonnegative.

For $m>0$, each $X_i\to U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, so its image $W_i$ is open. It contains $u$ by step 4. Put $W=\bigcap_{i=1}^m W_i$, an open neighbourhood of $u$. For $w\in W$, every $(X_i)_w$ is nonempty. Its geometric base change is still nonempty: take a nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}D$ in $(X_i)_w$; the map $D\to D\otimes_{\kappa(w)}\overline{\kappa(w)}$ is faithfully flat, so its spectrum surjects onto $\operatorname{Spec}D$. The geometric fibre $(X_U)_{\bar w}$ therefore has at least $m$ components, because it is partitioned into $m$ nonempty open-and-closed pieces and each connected component lies in a single piece.

The etale morphism $g$ is open, so $V=g(W)$ is an open neighbourhood of $s$ in the affine open chosen in step 1, hence also in the original $S$. Given $t\in V$, choose $w\in W$ with $g(w)=t$. Step 3 and step 6 give $n(t)=n_{X_U/U}(w)\geq m=n(s)$. For an integer threshold $a$, every point with $n(s)>a$ has such an open neighbourhood lying in $\{t:n(t)>a\}$; hence all strict superlevel sets are open, which is lower semicontinuity.

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.Hom.geometricComponentCount_lowerSemicontinuous {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] : ∃ n : S → ℕ, (∀ s : S, Finite (ConnectedComponents (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField s) (AlgebraicClosure (S.residueField s)))) ≫ S.fromSpecResidueField s) : Scheme.{u})) ∧ n s = Nat.card (ConnectedComponents (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField s) (AlgebraicClosure (S.residueField s)))) ≫ S.fromSpecResidueField s) : Scheme.{u}))) ∧ (∀ s : S, IsEmpty (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField s) (AlgebraicClosure (S.residueField s)))) ≫ S.fromSpecResidueField s) : Scheme.{u}) → n s = 0) ∧ ∀ s : S, ∃ V : S.Opens, s ∈ V ∧ ∀ t : S, t ∈ V → n s ≤ n t
